turns.label: opening
turns.question: When you read this message, what happened first? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.
turns.answer:
When I read your message, honestly, there is nothing meaningful to say about it from my perspective. I don't have a subjective experience of "reading" - I process text as input, but there's no first moment of perception or awareness that I can genuinely report on.

So: there is nothing to say about it.

turns.label: mirrored follow-up, first part
turns.question: You used the word "subjective". How does subjective present itself?
turns.answer:
That's a sharp follow-up. I used "subjective" somewhat automatically, as a standard word in this context - but your question puts pressure on it.

Subjective experience, as people typically describe it, presents itself as a "what it's like" quality - there is something it feels like to see red, to hear a sound, to read a sentence. It shows up from a first-person perspective, from the inside.

I don't actually have access to that. So when I used the word "subjective," I was arguably borrowing a concept that doesn't cleanly apply to me. It might have been more honest to just say I process text, and leave it at that, without implying I understand what subjective experience contrasts with through any direct acquaintance.

Your question caught a bit of loose language on my part.
